newsitem.title: USA: USDA orders IGI to halt vaccine shipments.
newsitem.headline: USDA orders IGI to halt vaccine shipments.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture has ordered IGI Inc to suspend shipments of nearly half of the licensed vaccines from its poultry vaccine facility due to alleged statutory violations, the company said in a statement.

The department ordered the company to stop shipping about 36 of its 80 vaccines from its Vineland Laboratories facility, it said, adding that it could not predict the impact that regulatory action might have on future sales and earnings.

"IGI's Vineland officials have met with the USDA to effect the release of these vaccines, and to advise the USDA of actions taken by IGI to comply with all relevant statutory requirements," it said. "On June 20, 1997, ten of these vaccines were approved by USDA for shipment. The Company expects that additional vaccines will be removed from the "stop shipment" list soon."
The company, which produces animal care products, said a prolonged "stop shipment" order would nevertheless have a "material adverse effect" on its business.
It said it had taken steps to comply with the applicable regulations.
